title: Coin pickup sparkle
prompt:
A 0.5-second game coin / collectible pickup, 24,000 samples at 48 kHz stereo, 30 fps, onset on frame 0, instantly readable as "collect": its own two-note-ish sparkle. LEGAL RULES: do NOT use the B5 -> E6 pattern or ANY rising perfect fourth between the two main notes; do not use 987.8 Hz or 1318.5 Hz; do not use a plain square/pulse-wave chip voice with the 'short note then held higher note' rhythm; not modelled on any game's sound. Bright but not piercing (keep energy above 10 kHz low), centred core with a little stereo sparkle, no low end, silent before 0.48 s.

Take angle 1 (glass bell, rising major sixth): D6 (1174.7 Hz) for ~45 ms then B6 (1975.5 Hz) ringing; timbre is a soft two-operator FM glass bell (c:m 1:3.5, index decaying fast) plus 5-6 tiny inharmonic sparkle pings scattered in stereo over ~150 ms after the second note.
notes:
Legal-safe redo: a 45 ms D6 then a ringing B6 (a rising major sixth) on a soft two-operator FM glass bell (c:m 1:3.5, fast-decaying index), plus six tiny inharmonic sparkle pings scattered in stereo over ~150 ms.
FFT-verified: no B5→E6, no rising perfect fourth, nothing at 987.8 or 1318.5 Hz, and no square/pulse chip voice; energy above 10 kHz is 36.6 dB down, silent from 0.48 s.
Take 1 of 3 (glass bell), picked as the most distinctive and furthest from any existing game sound; replaces the earlier B5→E6 chip coin.
